agent_notes: The Hebrew verse 1 carries the superscription 'Song of the Ascents' (KJV 126:0) together with the first line; I translated both as one verse. The key crux is בְּשׁוּב יְהוָה אֶת־שִׁיבַת צִיּוֹן: the versions split between 'turned again the captivity' (KJV, ASV, Webster), 'made a change in fate' (BBE) and 'brought back those who returned' (ASV). I kept the literal 'when YHWH returned the returning of Zion', which preserves the shuv/shivat wordplay and leaves open both readings (return of the exiles and reversal of fortune; shivat may be a variant of shevut, see Ibn Ezra and Radak). Radak and Metzudat David read the verb as transitive, Meiri also allows an intransitive 'when YHWH returns'.

The tense of the psalm is debated: היינו כחולמים is a perfect, read as past (return already happened: Webster/KJV 'were'), or as prophetic perfect for the future (Rashi, Radak, Meiri, Malbim treat it as the exile looking forward). The English can keep 'we were' in the literal layer; the dramatic layer follows the past-tense memory reading, which the later plea in verse 4 ('Return our fortunes') shows is not the whole story. I flagged the ambiguity in the commentary rather than resolving it.

agent_notes: Ketiv/Qere: written שבותנו (shevutenu), read שביתנו (shevitenu); STEPBible follows the reading. Glossed the reading as 'our captivity/fortunes' and mentioned the Ketiv in a note (Radak and Meiri both observe the vav/yod difference and say the sense is one). I translated 'restore our fortunes' only in the dramatic layer; the literal layer keeps 'captivity' as the lexicon form of the root, with 'fortunes' in the commentary.

אֲפִיקִים: 'stream-beds' / 'wadis' (HALOT, BDB) against KJV 'streams' and Ibn Ezra, Metzudat Zion 'strongly flowing water'. The image of the Negev wadi that is dry for most of the year and fills with flash flood after rain is my reading of the sense; the commentators in the packet stress the 'strength' of the flow (Ibn Ezra, Meiri) or the contrast with the dry land (Radak, Rashi).

agent_notes: מֶשֶׁךְ־הַזָּרַע is uncertain. The packet's commentators split: Ibn Ezra and Meiri 'the vessel/bag containing the seed', Radak 'the precious seed' (from drawing out/attracting; KJV follows with 'precious seed'), Metzudat Zion 'the drawing/carrying of the seed'. I translated 'the seed-bag' in both layers, because the participle 'carrying' fits a container, and said so in the commentary. The meaning of משך as 'bag' is attested only here, hence the note carries no lexicon citation.
Didn't cite BDB/HALOT page numbers anywhere in this window; the lexical claims I made (אפיק, נגב, אלמה) are standard but I give the lexicon name only without page or entry detail.
